=== Possible William Allen Glasgow, Royal Engineers commission, 1795 ===
Gentleman Cadet William Allen Glasgow is announced as second lieutenant in the Corps of Royal Engineers, vice Lefebvre, promoted, dated 1 October 1795.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395720951/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1795-10-15, p.4].</ref>

The commission date is 1 October 1795, not the 15 October publication day. "Gentleman Cadet" describes his prior status; the notice gives no parents, birthplace or subsequent career. A William without a recorded middle name remains a possible identification.

This may concern [[Glasgow-1463]]. Broad uncertain before 25 February 1816 birth is not an exact year and permits adulthood in 1795. It supplies no Allen, age or officer identification.

=== Possible William Glasgow, Cleugh-head and Clovenfordsyke tenancy notices, 1774–1777 ===
William Glasgow, tenant and co-possessor with William Wilson of Cleugh-head and Clovenfordsyke, is named in a planned land-sale notice at John’s coffee-house, Edinburgh, for 31 July 1776.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/601811451/ The Edinburgh Advertiser, 1776-06-28, p.6].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/601811628/ The Edinburgh Advertiser, 1776-07-02, p.8].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/601812065/ The Edinburgh Advertiser, 1776-07-12, p.8].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/601812638/ The Edinburgh Advertiser, 1776-07-26, p.8].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/601812762/ The Edinburgh Advertiser, 1776-07-30, p.7].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395682789/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1776-06-26, p.3].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395684189/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1776-07-10, p.4].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395684792/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1776-07-17, p.4].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395687327/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1776-07-26, p.4].</ref>

William Glasgow, tenant and co-possessor with William Wilson of Cleugh-head and Clovenfordsyke, is named in a planned land-sale notice at John’s coffee-house, Edinburgh, for 28 August 1776, by adjournment.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/601813064/ The Edinburgh Advertiser, 1776-08-06, p.7].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/601813385/ The Edinburgh Advertiser, 1776-08-13, p.7].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/601813701/ The Edinburgh Advertiser, 1776-08-20, p.8].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/601813994/ The Edinburgh Advertiser, 1776-08-27, p.7].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395690561/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1776-08-19, p.4].</ref>

William Glasgow is tenant/possessor of Cleugh-head and Clovenfordsyke lots in a sale advertisement planning a roup on 5 January 1775; his tack is stated to expire at Martinmas 1776.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395699867/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1774-12-12, p.3].</ref>

William Glasgow is named as former possessor of the Cleugh-head haughs in a further adjourned land-sale notice planning 17 September 1777.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395689234/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1777-08-30, p.4].</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395690882/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1777-09-13, p.4].</ref>

The notices describe planned sales, an adjournment and later former possession, not a completed transaction. The named farms support one provisional tenancy sequence; no family relationship with William Wilson is stated.

This may concern [[Glasgow-1463]]. Broad before-1816 birth boundary permits 1776, but provides no age, tenancy or family connection; weak comparison.
